decks.name: LeetCode #1448 - Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
decks.description: Count nodes where value is greater than or equal to all values in path from root

cards.question: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree: Given a binary tree root, a node X in the tree is named good if in the path from root to X there are no nodes with a value greater than X. Return the number of good nodes in the binary tree.

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use recursive DFS to traverse tree while tracking maximum value seen in current path from root. A node is good if its value is greater than or equal to max value in path. For each node, check if good, update max value, then recursively count good nodes in left and right subtrees. Sum counts from both subtrees. O(n) time and space.

solutions.timeDescription: Linear time as each node is visited exactly once during depth-first traversal
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack proportional to tree height, O(h) typically, O(n) worst case for skewed tree
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given tree [3,1,4,3,null,1,5]: dfs(3,3): good, res=1. dfs(1,3): 1<3 not good, res=0. dfs(3,3): good, res=1. dfs(4,3): good, res=1. dfs(1,4): 1<4 not good, res=0. dfs(5,4): good, res=1. Total: 1+0+1+1+0+1=4 good nodes.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use BFS with queue storing (node, maxVal) pairs. Initialize queue with root and negative infinity. For each node, check if value is at least maxVal (making it good), increment count if so. Add children to queue with updated maxVal as max of current maxVal and node value. Process until queue empty. O(n) time and space.
